title: Overprint
description: Three huge numerals in process red, blue and yellow race up a shallow diagonal across paper-white stock, each a translucent ink laid over the others. Where they cross the inks multiply like a real press run: red over blue goes aubergine, red over yellow goes vermilion, blue over yellow goes green, all three go a warm brown-black. At speed a numeral prints its pace the way Huber did, as flat hard-edged bands of its own ink trailing behind it. The plates are cut at three sizes and share one oblique: a small 0 down on the bottom edge, an 8 bigger than the sheet that runs off its top and leading side, and a 5 that never rests in its slot. Its home is a break, out ahead of the others with its rules running back at full length across the open stock it left, so the sheet at rest is already the race. Every few seconds one of the other two plates breaks away, overtakes it and takes the lead, laps in over the trailing edge and drops back into its slot; only the fastest plate rules its pace in full, the others print short hairlines. Pick one up and its plate comes up a touch, flat ink still, no shadow; pull it out of register or throw it, and it races on at the pace you gave it, then falls back into its slot.
intent: After Max Huber's Monza race posters (Gran Premio dell'Autodromo 1948, 500 Miglia di Monza 1957), where transparent primary inks overprint so numbers and speed bands mix into new colours as they cross. https://a-g-i.org/design/500-miglia-di-monza
